extracted.intended_audience: researchers, journal editors, and those interested in publication ethics and retractions
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating expectations for how journals and editors should handle and explain retractions, and related institutional responses to research misconduct. Focused on transparency, adherence to publishing-ethics guidelines (e.g., COPE), and accountability for investigators and organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain reasons for retraction (COPE recommendation)
rubrics_metrics.description: COPE recommends explaining why papers were retracted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes the journal is a member of COPE and COPE "recommends explaining why papers were retracted." This implies retraction notices should include a clear statement of the reason(s) for the retraction rather than a bare notice. The author criticizes the journal for not providing such an explanation and has contacted the editor for clarification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor accountability: provide explanation when retracting
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors should offer an explanation when retracting papers; failing to do so is criticized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The post states, "That doesn’t excuse the editors from offering an explanation, and we’re curious why they decided against doing so." The surrounding implication is that editors bear a responsibility to inform readers why a retraction occurred (e.g., fabrication, error, authorship issue) and that omission is an editorial shortcoming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not tolerate or cover up misconduct (preserve public trust)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tolerance, turning a blind eye, or covering up obvious misconduct erodes public trust in science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A commenter summarizes this standard: closing one’s eyes/years (not to offend colleague, not to open a can of worms, not to give ammunition to critics) or worse—cover up—can only erode the public trust in science, beyond the individual actor. This functions as a normative criterion for institutions and journals when confronting suspected misconduct: act transparently and decisively rather than tolerate or conceal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational compliance and enforcement of principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of organizations (e.g., COPE) should adhere to the organization's frameworks/principles/guidelines; there should be consequences when they do not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A commenter asks what should happen to members who do not adhere to an organisation’s framework/principles/guidelines, implying a standard that professional organizations must enforce their own rules and that membership implies compliance obligations. This suggests journals and societies should have mechanisms to ensure and enforce compliance with ethical guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate and pursue legal/administrative consequences for fraud
rubrics_metrics.description: Research fraud—especially involving funded grants—may warrant formal investigation and possible legal or administrative penalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A commenter notes the FIOD (Dutch fiscal/investigative authority) announced an investigation into Stapel for fraud and deceit because he received government-funded research grants, suggesting that serious misconduct should trigger external investigations and potential criminal or administrative sanctions beyond retraction. This frames a criterion that addressing misconduct may require involvement of law enforcement or funding agencies.
